facts.statement: malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 to npm and a trojanized Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 release on GitHub.
Treat the machine as compromised. Move the Swarm node’s funds and stake to a new key. Treat the old key as stolen.
Any computer that has this package installed or running should be considered fully compromised.

editorial.title: Malicious bee-js and Swarm Desktop releases abuse a trusted release path
editorial.summary: Socket and SafeDep report malicious @ethersphere/bee-js 13.3.0 and Swarm Desktop 0.56.2 releases delivering remote-code loaders. The npm package carried valid provenance; affected systems need compromise assessment, not just a package downgrade.
editorial.why_it_matters: Release provenance can faithfully attest to malicious code built through a compromised workflow. Swarm node wallet keys and persistent backdoors are part of the reported impact.
editorial.action: Check install and launcher history. Isolate affected systems, rotate exposed credentials from a clean machine, and follow the researchers’ wallet-key and persistence-removal guidance.
